newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH DSM TO REPORT FLAT Q1 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH DSM TO REPORT FLAT Q1 PROFIT.

text.p: High prices for plastics raw materials in the first two months of 1997 have pressured first-quarter results at Dutch petrochemicals group DSM, but analysts are divided on the overall impact on the bottom line.
First-quarter net profit from ordinary operations is forecast at 185 million to 233 million guilders, with the consensus at 217 million. DSM is due to report on Tuesday.
Last year DSM posted first-quarter net from ordinary operations of 216 million before a one million guilder minority charge and a 10 million guilder one-off loss.
"I expect some pressure on margins, particularly in the cyclically sensitive hydrocarbons and polymers activities," said Nils van Elzelingen of NIB Securities.
He said that while sales prices for plastics had risen, this would have been countered by high prices for naphtha, a raw material, which only started falling in late February.
Van Elzelingen expected first-quarter ordinary net of 214 million guilders.
ING Barings' Quirijn Mulder was more upbeat, forecasting 237 million guilders.

"Naphtha prices started falling later in the quarter, while selling prices were consistently higher than in the previous quarter," he said. Currency effects would also have boosted operating earnings.

DSM does not publish a breakdown of results per sector in its quarterly report, but analysts were agreed that the biggest influence on group earnings would be the developments at its core hydrocarbons and polymers activities.
The other divisions (industrial and fine chemicals, resins and plastic products and energy) will largely have performed in line with previous quarters, they said.
